content: A sword never kills anybody; it is a tool in the killer's hand.
author: Seneca
sourceWork: De Tranquillitate Animi (On Tranquility of Mind)
story:
There is a sharp, grounded clarity in this observation. True wisdom is rarely complicated or flashy, but it demands the honesty to look at our own habits and assumptions without defensive excuses.

Seneca understood that real peace is never won by escaping the world or blaming external circumstances. When you stop looking for external validation and anchor your self-worth in quiet integrity, the noisy chaos of the world loses its power over you. A good life is built day by day through small, conscious choices.
reflectionPrompt: How does adopting this philosophical view alter the way you handle current friction?
